b2d3e985b344df72b5d6c8e5b13134cd720cfaa9.summary: This is a Chinese-language forum post sharing a Windows credential-dumping utility, GetPwd_K8, described as built on the open-source mimikatz tool. It says the utility recovers plaintext logon passwords on Windows XP through Windows 7 and Server 2008, and it lists four builds with file sizes and hashes. The post says the builds are meant to help with antivirus evasion. The text is a tool-distribution post, not a threat analysis report, so no facts are recorded.

b2386bef6e70b932af44e6bb3f3d3f1cc3cc69ec.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reports on how threat actors use AI across the attack lifecycle. It describes AI-assisted vulnerability research and exploit development, including a zero-day it believes was AI-developed, and AI-enabled malware such as PROMPTSPY that uses an LLM to control an Android device. It also covers AI-generated decoy code and obfuscation, AI-augmented reconnaissance and information operations, and scaled illicit access to LLMs through middleware and account pooling. Supply chain attacks on AI software, including the LiteLLM compromise by TeamPCP, are covered…

hedges: GTIG believes the zero-day exploit was developed with AI, and its counter discovery may have prevented the planned mass exploitation.
The report does not believe Gemini was used for the zero-day, but has high confidence an AI model was used.
Malware is linked to suspected Russia-nexus threat actors.
The report assesses PROMPTSPY's LLM component was designed to be extensible and was likely designed for multiple device interaction types.
The report says the APT27 fleet management application is likely to support an ORB network, and the CANFAIL and LONGSTREAM decoy code was likely added for obfuscation.
The Operation Overload voice cloning is suspected and likely represents an AI-supported advancement of the campaign's established tactics.
Many AI uses are described as experimental; the report has not identified the generated IO content in the wild and says none created breakthrough capabilities.
The report says threat actors have not yet achieved breakthrough capabilities to bypass the core security logic of frontier models.
